attribution.path: crates/drift-mine/src/mine.rs:4671-4679 (variant_set drops non-guard alternatives) then mine.rs:4798-4806 (across_depths, CHILD_MARGIN mine.rs:35)
attribution.detail: Base mined modules/** as a variant set that included the unauthenticated actionClient (D-60208a). #60 keeps only guard alternatives, so the parent becomes the single wrapper authenticatedActionClient.inputSchema().action at 107/119 (Wilson lb 0.832). Its child modules/ee (56/58, lb 0.883) is 0.0507 higher, past CHILD_MARGIN 0.05, so dedupe step 3 drops the parent. The sibling join that would have widened the parent to authenticatedActionClient.action runs only after dedupe (mine.rs:2704). No convention covers the 61 server actions in modules/** outside modules/ee. Confirmed: with one extra unwrapped action in modules/ee (fb-01 applied) the child falls to lb 0.861 and the parent comes back as D-cf72ae (109/120).

attribution.pr: #49 (lazy-imports, F2), with the existing signal-seeded layering candidates
attribution.path: crates/drift-mine/src/mine.rs:377 (lazy/optional loads emit no import signal) and mine.rs:3633-3639 (avoid_drafts seeds candidates only from signals some member has)
attribution.detail: packages/core's only imports of platform-express, websockets and microservices are lazy loads of declared optional peers. #49 rightly stops counting them as violations (v3: all three WRONG). But layering candidates are seeded only from import signals that some member of the role has. With no signal left, the rule is never generated, and a static relative import of ../../platform-express is not reported. Even if it were seeded, consider() (mine.rs:4578) would drop a rule that 203/203 members hold as universal.
